To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MEVVA source is capable of delivering a high current uranium ion beam to a transport system and that the RFQ can accelerate uranium ion beams to 3.6 MeV/u.

the MEVVA source is capable of providing high current ion beams for transport through a beam transport channel and for acceleration in a single-gap column, and that the RFQ can accelerate a uranium beam to an energy of 2 MeV.

the MEVVA high current ion source has successfully produced uranium beams of sufficient current and quality for use in the GSI RFQ, that the RFQ has been successfully tested with uranium as the injected species, and that the RFQ is capable of accelerating uranium beams to energies in excess of 100 kV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production and transport of high current ion beams, and with their subsequent acceleration.
the production and acceleration of intense beams of heavy ions.
the development of a heavy ion beam injector system for the SNS, and with the development of an injector for the proposed ESS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MEVVA source has been successfully tested in an accelerator environment, and the RFQ has been successfully operated with uranium as the accelerating species. the MEVVA source has been successfully tested in an injector environment.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of the MEVUA ion source in an injection system, the feasibility of the RFQ in an injector environment and the feasibility of transporting uranium beams through a high voltage accelerating column.

The main takeaway from our work is that
MEVVA beams are well-suited for transport through long beam transport channels.
uranium ions can be efficiently extracted from the source and accelerated to high energy in a single-gap accelerating tube.

the MEVVA source can provide beams of uranium with high current and low emittance, which are well matched to the RFQ linac, and that these beams can be transported to and accelerated in a conventional RFQ.
